newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Congress condemns photographer's murder.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Congress condemns photographer's murder.

text.p: Argentina's Congress on Wednesday condemned the brutal murder of a news photographer as police seemed to make headway in solving the crime.

Jose Luis Cabezas was shot and his handcuffed body incinerated in his car on January 25. The crime sparked a wave of protests from journalists over threats to their profession and revived grim memories of the political violence which rocked Argentina during military rule in the 1970s.

"These events and threats specifically directed at journalists which have still not been solved generate a climate of unease and tension which do not contribute to the strengthening of democratic institutions," said a statement signed by all members of Congress.
The last time both chambers of Argentina's Congress met to jointly declare their grave concern was in April 1987, after a barracks uprising against President Raul Alfonsin.
There were also signs of progress in the investigation, which has been marred by allegations of police inefficiency.

President Carlos Menem was informed on Wednesday by investigators that a pistol found when five suspects were arrested earlier this week was the weapon used to kill the 35-year-old father of three, the state-run Telam news agency reported.

Cabezas's charred body was found in his car at Pinamar, a beach resort town popular with the rich and politicians where he was covering the holiday season. He worked for Noticias, a sometimes controversial weekly.

His murder provoked a storm of protest from journalists and local and international press organisations. It has also embarrassed the Peronist government of President Carlos Menem and the police, which have failed to solve a string of high-profile cases, most notably the bloody bombing of a Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires in 1994.
